commits.message:
Count mint-item-non-canonical among the shared assembly's definitions

Mint now carries its family definition in the registry, so the shared
assembly table builds it like the other cursor families. The table no
longer lists it as separately assembled, counts 31 cursor definitions,
and gives it the same config-and-material runtime fixture as the other
authenticated-certificate families.

Refs #905

Advance an idle stack's ended scheduler shift before funding the ledger owner

On an idle stack no node commits, so none advances the scheduler, and its
datum keeps a shift that ended long ago. The ledger owner's funding gate
waited for some operator to move it and failed at its deadline: twin4's
long drill stopped there, before any family, on a datum 32 hours stale.

Who holds the next shift, and from when, is fixed only by the transaction
that advances it: an ended shift passes to its one successor, starting at
that transaction's validity start. A gate deciding on an ended datum is
deciding on a shift that does not exist yet. The funding gate now advances
an ended shift itself, through the node's own alignment with operator-2's
wallet, as each family's onboarding already does, and decides on the shift
that appoints. After our node's ended shift that is operator-2's, where the
deposit is held to the floor and falls due too late for a strike; after
operator-2's it is our node's, where the deposit is published at once. A
refresh another operator's advance overtakes decides on that advance; one
that fails while the scheduler stays put refuses.

The refresh signs as operator-2, whose wallet signs only while the drill
holds its node stopped, and funding runs before any family takes that
hold. The gate therefore takes it just before it advances the scheduler;
a funding that advances nothing leaves operator-2 running.

The funding refuses ahead of its deadline rather than past it: before a
retry the node holds not yet due, and before waiting for operator-2's
floor, whenever either would end after the deadline.

The family user-event gate and the funding admission now refuse an ended
shift instead of deciding on it.

Name the CEK core routing golden's Aiken output in one path literal

The preflight derives a golden channel's triggers from the whole path
literals its generator names. The routing generator joined the output's
directory and file name separately, so the channel named no .ak file and
an Aiken edit could not select it. Write the path whole, as the core-step
generator does.

Judge our node's hold on the fault by the watcher's removal, not the fault's first spend

Two ways an honest stack drill could fail after its fault was proven and
removed.

While a block is unattested our node reports an invalid block only as
awaiting its DA (#925), and nothing makes the watcher's fraud removal wait
for the DA apply. A fault removed before its attestation was therefore
never reported invalid, and the successor stage failed with "never
reported landed_block_invalid". Observable 1 now accepts a fault held only
awaiting its DA when, and only when, Kupo shows the watcher's removal at a
slot strictly before the fault's DA apply, or no DA apply at all. The
family records this as its own stage,
held-awaiting-da-removed-before-attestation, with the removal and the
apply (or none) as evidence, and the result verifier refuses that stage
unless the removal is the correction's own, at the slot the chain shows,
and any apply lies strictly after it. Every other awaiting-only case fails
as before.

The window in which our node held the fault as the tail took the fault's
oldest state-queue output's spend as its removal. For an attested fault
that spend is the DA apply, which comes before our node's first invalid
report, so the window was always empty: the family passed only if our
node happened to report a pending commit, a fault removed before our
shift failed instead of being recorded as not reached, and the measured
commit-to-conviction time was the apply's. The removal is now the fault
output spent by the watcher's removal transaction, the one the correction
authenticated; the window, the removal evidence and
faultCommitToConvictionMs all use its slot. When Kupo shows no spend by
that transaction the removal is not proven and the window ends where the
fault left the queue.

Each family's result now also records the fault's attestation lag after
its block time, or null with no DA apply, so the long run measures the
race between attestation and removal.

Declare the nine direct-walk families once and drive them through one kit port

Each direct-walk family carried its own transaction port, a workflow
module of five names over the shared assembly, and a hand-written
application record. The kit now has defineDirectWalkFamily, one
transaction port with no category branch, and directWalkApplicationRecord.
Each family's workflow module declares only its walk: spec, family,
artifact and replay. The nine ports and the per-family aliases are
deleted, and the missing-redeemer and script-integrity-hash-mismatch
records move beside the other seven.

The port opens a page's carriage at the page start for every family,
since the fit builds each transaction of the page there. No family's
page tail opens a field today, so the opened sets are unchanged: a dump
of 694 custody captures across the transcript and the nine lifecycle
suites matched field for field, and the transcript hash is unchanged.

Refs #906

Route the fault-proof CEK planner and its group-7 branch from the chain table

The one-step planner kept its own lists of chains, semantic and staged
stages, failure tag ranges and kept-after stages, and ARMS_OF in the
max-shape case was a literal. All of them, and the holder lists and arm
contract names, are now derived once at load from the SDK chain table.
The facts kinds are rows.

Group 7's successor choice is a row too. It holds the tag limit, the
staged ranges, the writeBits loop tag and the 512-word limit, and
cekCoreFailureRoute reads it. The planner now refuses three group-7 steps
that the validators reject:
- a builtin tag above 86;
- a staged-failure writeBits witness over an input of at most 512 words;
- a writeBits failure over more than 512 words.

The routing golden gains group-7 rows for every tag at 512 and 513 words,
plus the two refused tags, each spending the real
semantic-failure-roots validator. A routes test covers each arm, tag and
size class, and the write-bits loop file now runs a 4,096-byte input that
fails mid-list. Compiled validators are unchanged.

Refs #892

Move the direct purpose artifact admission and plan memo into the kit

Each of the nine direct purpose families kept an artifact module and a
plan module of its own, which repeated the same admission checks, plan
memo and source inclusion. The kit now does all four once, in
direct-purpose-family/artifact.ts. Each family declares its admission and
proof as one X_ARTIFACT_FAMILY in its replay module, with the artifact
version written as a literal. The types and the declaring helper sit in a
leaf module with no runtime imports, so a family's replay module never
loads the complete replay. Admission runs the same checks in the same
order, with the same messages. The memo keeps its key and its limit per
family, and still evicts a failed plan. The journey script-cases test
prepares every family's artifact through one kit call, and a new test pins
each family's label and artifact version.

Refs #906

Build the prepared validation transaction once behind a pre-state ledger port

Prepare derived the proof source, committed fields, resolution schedule,
signer set, script sources, outputs and redeemers while it walked, and
complete reached back into prepare's locals. Those derivations now run
once, before the walk, in prepared-validation-transaction.ts. The result
is readonly by type. Prepare hands complete a readonly walk state, and
complete computes its source and purpose leaves once rather than once
per phase.

Input resolution proves against a PreStateLedger. Validation's adapter
builds the trie from the ledger witness entries, as before. The
fault-proofs adapter proves against the checked ledger's own trie, so a
dispute replay no longer rebuilds one. A test pins both adapters to
byte-equal proofs, absent keys included. The transcript and the witness
bytes are unchanged. The builders' size ceilings are lowered to their new
sizes.

Refs #908

Bound the drill's attested-tail reads by the first tail they see

The drill's attested-tail read polled the queue's last block and bounded
the wait by that block's own attestation timeout. The contract lets
blocks be appended to an unattested tail, so a stack that keeps
appending faster than the committee attests replaced the tail, and with
it the bound, at every poll. Inside the pre-run hook, which has no
timeout of its own, that wait could hang the run.

The read is now split by what each caller needs.

The two funded checks, in the pre-run hook (stack-ledger-owner.ts) and
before a family's onboarding (staging.journey-da-path.ts:179), pin the
tail at their first poll. They return the newest attested block at or
after it, within the pinned block's own bound of twice the DA
attestation timeout. A pinned block that leaves the queue, or that
nothing at or after is attested for by then, refuses by name. On twin4
a block may only be merged a block maturity (15 minutes) after its block
time, past its attestation window, so a pinned block is seen attested
before it can be merged away; rehearsal's maturity is seven days.

The predecessor read (staging.journey-da-path.ts:183) still needs the
current tail itself attested, since the fault's commit consumes the real
tail. It now keeps the bound of the first unattested tail it saw and
refuses by name once that passes, rather than resetting with each new
tail. That refusal cannot fire in normal operation: the read runs only
after onboardOperator() returns, which waits until the scheduler
appoints operator-2 and ledger time passes that shift's start
(published-block-actor.operator-shift.ts:66-73). Operator-2's node is
held stopped from before staging (journey-runner.attached-mode.ts:81),
no other operator can commit in that shift, and the read itself commits
nothing. So the tail cannot change while it waits, and it refuses only
when the committee neither attests nor removes that block within twice
its attestation timeout, which is a committee failure. A lone tail that
ages out keeps its old message.

Run mint-item-non-canonical on the shared retained-DA runner and delete its bridge

The registry row now carries the mint family definition, so mint runs on
the shared runner like every other family and joins the generalised
conformance suite. The bespoke executor, its central-journal adapter
(about 1.1k lines), resolve-mint-item-by-another-record, the actuation-permit
controller's mint evidence branch, the watcher's mint funding-recovery
branch, step_03's unused carriage arguments and the adapter's size
exception are deleted, with the six tests that only exercised them.

A journal whose prepared artifact is not the generic envelope, such as one
written by the bespoke mint workflow, now fails the shared journal reader
with an error naming the workflow id, and startup holds that objective as
fault_proof_objective_unreadable; other objectives keep running. The watcher
README states the remedy. An architecture test allows only the orchestrator
and the funding-reservation permit to import the journal-writer verbs.

Refs #905

Stop the ledger owner's landing wait at its absorption deadline

The pre-run funding waited for its deposit to land on L1 until Kupo
showed it landed or expired. A Kupo that kept answering while its
checkpoint stalled before the deposit's validity end kept that wait
going without end, and the funding hook sets no Vitest timeout of its
own, so the run would hang with no named refusal.

The landing wait now ends at the deposit's existing absorption
deadline, its due time plus two shifts and the DA attestation timeout,
and a miss refuses the run by name before any family starts.

Derive the CEK core stage builder from one chain table

cek-core-chain.ts now describes the 44 core roles once, each with a next,
semantics or branch successor; group 7's three-way branch is a row. The
stage titles, the applied order, the hop counts and the entry hashes are
derived from it at module load, and building them throws on a cycle or on
successors at unequal distance from the settle. cek-core.ts keeps its
exported names and only applies the derived order to the blueprint.
Invariant tests pin the table's shape against the manifest family. The
applied-chain transcript is unchanged.

Refs #892

Move the trace walk's stops and replay comparison into one driver

The prepare and complete builders each decided where a walk stops and
compared their reason with the replayed one at scattered points. A driver,
trace-walk.ts, now owns the phase stops and the comparison, and
trace-replay.ts owns the replay it compares against. Replay steers a stop
only for arms the producer cannot find itself, which are the arms the old
code steered; observer order is tagged again at the script-precondition
phase, where the old code steered every arm. A producer-found arm that
replay rejects and the walk passes is a disagreement. The builders' size
ceilings are lowered to their new declaration sizes.

Refs #908

Pin the CEK core routing and applied chain before deriving it from a table

Deletes CEK_CORE_STAGE_REFERENCES, which had no consumer, and moves
cekCoreGroup into the SDK so the validation generator can import it.

Adds the cek-core-routing-v1 golden channel: vectors swept from the TS
core_group and semantic_group twins render a JSON fixture and an Aiken
test module that runs every routed and boundary-refused pair against
cek_semantic_chain. It is wired as a channel row, package scripts and a
Node CI step.

An SDK transcript test pins each core role's validator title and
parameter CBOR, with successor hashes written by role, plus the entry
roles and hop counts, and checks every role against its applied script
on the real blueprint. No validator source or compiled code changes.

Refs #892

Move the direct walk families onto the direct purpose kit's terminal and fit

The distinct-asset, execution-native-script, script-integrity-hash and
unused-script-witness families each kept a terminal and a fit of their own;
DAAL also kept a copy of the shared page halving loop. They now submit the
kit's one terminal and fit through a paging adapter,
withDirectPurposeWalkPages, which routes a page start to the family walk or
the shared source. Families whose conviction needs per-run data (SIHM's
material, USW's selection) build their verdict at the call, so the kit
types are unchanged. DAAL now convicts from the terminal state's bound,
as terminal.ak does. The finalize redeemers encode to the same bytes as
the deleted ones, and transaction bytes are unchanged.
